group.title: Home and daily life
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: A boring job you have to do regularly at home, like washing up.
examples: Taking out the trash is my least favorite {chore}.
wrong: Watching TV is my favorite chore.

words.meaning: The work of cleaning and looking after a home.
examples: We share the {housework} equally.
wrong: I did the housework by sleeping on the sofa all day.

words.meaning: To clean floors with an electric machine that sucks up dirt.
examples: I {vacuumed} the carpet before the guests came.
wrong: I vacuumed the carpet by spilling crumbs all over it.

words.meaning: To clean a floor by brushing dirt away.
examples: Can you {sweep} the kitchen floor?
wrong: I swept the floor by throwing more sand on it.

words.meaning: To wash a floor with a wet cloth or sponge on a stick.
examples: She {mopped} the floor after the dog came in muddy.
wrong: He mopped the floor to make it dirtier.

words.meaning: Clothes and sheets that need washing or have just been washed.
examples: I do the {laundry} every Saturday.
wrong: The laundry is the meal we eat on Sundays.

words.meaning: To make clothes smooth with a hot, flat tool.
examples: I need to {iron} my shirt for the interview.
wrong: I ironed my shirt so it would be full of creases.

words.meaning: To bend cloth or paper so one part lies on top of another.
examples: Please {fold} the towels and put them away.
wrong: She folded the sheet by throwing it on the floor.

words.meaning: To make a place neat by putting things where they belong.
examples: Please {tidy up} your room before dinner.
wrong: I tidied up by throwing my toys all over the floor.

words.meaning: A machine used at home, such as a washing machine or toaster.
examples: The kitchen has all the modern {appliances}.
wrong: A chair is the most useful appliance in our kitchen.

words.meaning: A machine that washes plates, cups and pans.
examples: Put the dirty plates in the {dishwasher}.
wrong: I put my clothes in the dishwasher to dry them.

words.meaning: A machine that washes clothes.
examples: Put your jeans in the {washing machine}.
wrong: We keep the milk cold in the washing machine.

words.meaning: A piece of furniture or a space in a wall with a door and shelves, for storing things.
examples: The cups are in the {cupboard} above the sink.
wrong: We sleep in the cupboard because it has the softest bed.

words.meaning: A box that slides in and out of a piece of furniture, used for keeping things.
examples: My socks are in the top {drawer}.
wrong: I opened the drawer by pushing it further in.

words.meaning: A tall cupboard where you hang clothes.
examples: Hang your coat in the {wardrobe}.
wrong: I keep my car in the wardrobe.

words.meaning: A piece of thick cloth that covers part of a floor.
examples: There’s a soft {rug} in front of the fire.
wrong: The rug hangs on the window to keep out the light.

words.meaning: A piece of cloth that hangs over a window to block light or stop people seeing in.
examples: Close the {curtains} at night.
wrong: I closed the curtains to let more sunlight in.

words.meaning: The thing you turn to make water come out, for example over a sink.
examples: Turn off the {faucet} when you brush your teeth.
wrong: I turned on the faucet to stop the water.

words.meaning: A room or space just under the roof of a house.
examples: We keep old boxes in the {attic}.
wrong: We went down to the attic under the house.

words.meaning: A room or floor of a building that is below the ground.
examples: The washing machine is down in the {basement}.
wrong: From the basement we had a great view over the roofs.

words.meaning: The passage inside a house that leads to the rooms.
examples: Leave your shoes in the {hallway}.
wrong: We cooked dinner in the hallway’s oven.

words.meaning: A set of steps inside a building, with its rails.
examples: A wide {staircase} leads to the bedrooms.
wrong: We took the staircase to stay on the same floor.

words.meaning: An area of short grass in a yard or park.
examples: The kids played on the {lawn}.
wrong: We parked the car on the kitchen lawn.

words.meaning: To cut grass with a machine.
examples: Dad {mows} the lawn every Sunday.
wrong: He mowed the lawn to make the grass grow longer.

words.meaning: The usual things you do every day, in the same order.
examples: Coffee and a walk are part of my morning {routine}.
wrong: My routine changes completely every single day.

words.meaning: To sleep longer than you planned and wake up late.
examples: I {overslept} and missed the bus.
wrong: I overslept, so I was up an hour early.

words.meaning: A short sleep during the day.
examples: Grandpa has a {nap} after lunch.
wrong: He had a nap that lasted all night and the next day.

words.meaning: Untidy and dirty, with things all over the place.
examples: Your bedroom is really {messy}.
wrong: The kitchen was messy, with everything clean and in its place.

words.meaning: Completely clean.
examples: After the party the house was {spotless} again.
wrong: The floor was spotless, covered in mud and crumbs.

words.meaning: To let water or gas escape through a hole or crack.
examples: The pipe under the sink is {leaking}.
wrong: The bucket leaked, so it stayed full all day.

words.meaning: A person whose job is fixing water pipes, sinks and toilets.
examples: We called a {plumber} to fix the leaking pipe.
wrong: The plumber cut my hair.

words.meaning: A dirty or untidy state.
examples: The kids made a big {mess} in the kitchen.
wrong: There was a mess, so everything was neat and clean.

words.meaning: A brush with a long handle for cleaning floors.
examples: Use the {broom} to sweep up the leaves.
wrong: I brushed my teeth with a broom.

words.meaning: A liquid or powder used for washing clothes or dishes.
examples: Add some {detergent} to the washing machine.
wrong: I put detergent in my soup to add flavor.

words.meaning: To take a cable out of the electric socket in the wall.
examples: {Unplug} the iron when you’ve finished.
wrong: I unplugged the lamp to turn it on.

words.meaning: A system that keeps a building warm.
examples: Turn on the {heating}; it’s freezing in here.
wrong: We turned on the heating to cool the house down.

words.meaning: All the people who live together in one home.
examples: There are five people in our {household}.
wrong: Our household is the road outside our building.

words.meaning: Lots of things lying around untidily.
examples: Clear the {clutter} off your desk.
wrong: The room had no clutter, just piles of junk everywhere.

words.meaning: To clean something by rubbing it hard with a brush or cloth.
examples: I {scrubbed} the pan to get the burnt food off.
wrong: She scrubbed the floor by gently looking at it.

words.meaning: To clean a surface by rubbing it with a cloth.
examples: Please {wipe} the table after dinner.
wrong: I wiped the table with a cloth to make it sticky.
